subject: Kickoff: ISO/FedRAMP readiness - evidence checkpoints and next steps
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@secureaudits.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-31T15:22:00Z
Subject: Kickoff: ISO/FedRAMP evidence intake

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for agreeing to run the intake with us. To get the kickoff scheduled, can you confirm the primary in-scope services and provide the following by next week: a preliminary inventory of in-scope systems, an architecture diagram, and an initial answers spreadsheet for SIG/CAIQ so we can triage gaps?

For FedRAMP we typically need a short note on encryption-in-transit/storage, KMS usage, and data residency boundaries up front. If you have someone technical who can join the kickoff, please CC them.

Proposed windows for a one-hour kickoff: Nov 3 (10–12 PST) or Nov 4 (14–16 PST).

Thanks,
Oliver Grant
Senior Engagement Lead
SecureAudits Inc.

Subject: Re: Kickoff: ISO/FedRAMP evidence intake

Hi Oliver — thanks, we can do this. Looping in Mina (security engineering) and Marissa (compliance program) to own the artifacts.

Quick answers up front:
- In-scope services: Redwood inference public API and Dedicated offering (control plane + inference runtime). Private deployments will be scoped per-customer and treated as out-of-scope for this baseline assessment — we can confirm if Acme needs private scope included.
- Encryption: TLS for in-transit; KMS-backed DEK for at-rest (AWS KMS/Customer-managed keys for dedicated).

I've attached our readiness-intake-template.xlsx to capture SIG/CAIQ answers and owners. Suggest we take the Nov 3 slot at 10:30 PST — that works for Mina and me. Marissa, can you confirm and add sprint windows for evidence collection?

Tessa Morgan
Head of Trust Operations | Redwood Inference

On Tue, Nov 3, 2026 at 08:05 Tessa Morgan wrote:
> Hi Oliver — thanks, we can do this. Looping in Mina (security engineering) and Marissa (compliance program) to own the artifacts.

Thanks — confirming 10:30 PST works and I'll join with two engineers who own the runtime and infra. Quick heads-up on what we'll bring to the kickoff:
- System architecture diagram (attached) that shows control plane, inference runtime, cache layers, and network boundaries.
- Access control matrix (attached) mapping role permissions to components (we'll mark sensitive roles with sampling owners).
- For FedRAMP: we will need auditor confirmation about whether dedicated capacity for customers (Dedicated) is in-scope as a managed service or as customer-managed. That drives evidence for multi-tenant isolation and network boundary proofs.

Action items I propose during kickoff:
1) Confirm scope (public API, Dedicated, Private)
2) Assign evidence owners and sample windows (teams + dates)
3) Agree on deliverables for SIG / CAIQ initial pass

Mina Haddad
Director, Security Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@secureaudits.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Kickoff: ISO/FedRAMP evidence intake — sprint plan proposal

Oliver / team — thanks for coordinating. After syncing internally, here's a pragmatic proposal for evidence collection to avoid repeated context switches:
- Sprint 1 (Nov 8–19): Architecture & control mapping artifacts (diagrams, ACL exports, identity provider configs).
- Sprint 2 (Nov 22–Dec 3): Operational evidence (logs, incident runbooks, patch records, config change history).
- Sprint 3 (Dec 6–17): Policy and personnel evidence (HR attestations, background checks sampling, training records).

Please advise expected sample sizes for ACLs, logs, and personnel (we typically plan for 5–10% sampling for personnel). We're aiming to deliver a packaged evidence bundle per sprint.

I've attached a short evidence-sprint-plan.pdf showing owners and proposed drop dates. Note: for ISO 27001 we'll need an internal audit window before certification activities; suggest we schedule that in parallel to Sprint 2.

Marissa Cole
Senior Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: evidence-sprint-plan.pdf (stub)
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@secureaudits.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T11:55:00Z
Subject: Re: Kickoff: ISO/FedRAMP evidence intake — sprint plan proposal

Marissa — the sprint cadence looks good. For sample guidance:
- Personnel: 5% acceptable for initial sampling, 10% if higher assurance is requested.
- ACL/permissions: provide a representative export for critical components (IAM roles, service accounts) plus 3 user-specific permission traces for each critical access path.
- Logs: 14–30 day windows for runbook verification, with at least three discrete incident/alert examples if available.

On FedRAMP scoping: for Dedicated we usually treat provider-managed Dedicated pools as in-scope if Redwood manages the capacity and the customer data traverses the same tenancy — but we can confirm after the kickoff once we see your architecture diagram.

I'll upload a working Drive folder and a follow-up questionnaire for SIG details; please post your completed intake spreadsheet there. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bsecure-audit-intake

Oliver

Thanks all — quick summary and next steps before the 10:30 PST kickoff today:
1) Confirmed scope for the kickoff: public API + Dedicated pools (we will flag Private deployments as customer-scoped unless Acme requests inclusion). Acme Security — please confirm if you want Private included.
2) Attachments to be uploaded to the Drive folder today: readiness-intake-template.xlsx, system-architecture-diagram.pdf, access-control-matrix.xlsx, evidence-sprint-plan.pdf, and a first-pass SIG/CAIQ draft (sig-caix-summary-draft.docx).
3) Owners: Mina — runtime/infra evidence; Marissa — compliance packaging and retention policies; Tessa — coordination and auditor questions.
4) FedRAMP note: we'll clarify Dedicated scoping in the kickoff and capture the decision in the meeting notes.

Proposed next actions after kickoff: assign per-artifact owners in JIRA (SUP-4521), Marissa to publish sprint drop calendar, Mina to prepare ACL exports for Sprint 1.

Meeting: Nov 7, 10:30–11:30 PST (Zoom link in calendar invite).

Please reply with any concerns; otherwise we'll proceed as above.

Tessa Morgan
Head of Trust Operations | Redwood Inference
